# 2025 REEFSCAPE – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- Dominant solution: **ground CORAL intake**. Many robots could place on all levels and take ALGAE from the REEF
  or the floor and score it in the NET.
- Elite play was decided by **L1 expertise and ALGAE in the NET**. The third robot was either another scorer or a
  defender.
- Elite human players introduced CORAL so it landed closer to the REEF, and sometimes directed it to a desired
  location.
- Almost all top robots climbed the **DEEP CAGE**.

## Dominant robots
- **1690, 2056, 4414** – star-wheel CORAL ground intake feeding inner straightening wheels that lay the CORAL in a
  tray at the bottom of the robot, ready for the rotating arm on the elevator to grab it (handoff). 1690 and 4414
  used a sideways elevator, 2056 a regular elevator. 2056 and 4414 had a two-side-roller gripper that could also
  take ALGAE from the floor, not just from the REEF; 1690 used a vacuum gripper. They could place CORAL and ALGAE
  anywhere, and CORAL on both sides.
- **1778** – wide ground CORAL intake that collapses and hands off to a simple end effector handling both CORAL and
  ALGAE; CORAL is held perpendicular to the intake; places on both sides.
- **1323** – another very complex 1323 robot: a utility arm (elevator on a low pivot) whose end effector has two
  more DOF. CORAL ground intake that can place directly on L1 or hand off to the arm. Grippy wheels on the elevator
  hold the CAGE, and the DEEP climb is done by rotating the low pivot.
- **2910** – their signature utility arm (rotation at the base, a telescopic arm on it, another rotation for the end
  effector). End effector with separate grippy orthogonal wheels that can hold an ALGAE ball, and hold CORAL wide
  for L1 or straightened inside for L2–L4. Grippy wheels on the telescope hold the CAGE; DEEP climb by rotating the
  arm.
- **422, 604, 3683, 1796, 7457** – a huge slide from the human-player station (lots of room for human-player error)
  into a dual-purpose end effector on the elevator (all on a wrist) that can hold CORAL and ALGAE at the same time;
  could place anywhere.
- **5940, 1678** – sideways elevator with an end effector that holds both pieces at once, plus a ground CORAL
  intake. The end effector could also rotate. ALGAE / CORAL placement on the side opposite the CORAL intake.

## Effective mechanisms
- **2630** – 971-2018-style two-DOF arm with two wheels and a wrist motor.
- **1778 intake** – wide top and bottom rollers with active centering belts inside: it centres the CORAL so that
  when the intake collapses it hands off to the end effector, which places orthogonal to the intake (both sides).
- **1690 / 2056 / 4414 star-wheel intake** – floating front roller plus an inner straightening mechanism (flap-down
  pivot or 4-bar deployment).
- **1778 / 2056 end effector** – simple and effective side-wheel end effector.
- **5990 intake** – looks like a closed box with front top & bottom rollers and passive centering; collapses and
  hands off to the end effector, which places CORAL on the other side.
- **694 / 422** – dedicated L1 CORAL mechanism: a wide ground intake that can also place on L1.
- **1323** – dual-purpose wide ground intake: hand off to the end effector or place on L1.
- **254** – mechanical alignment on the REEF pole, then release.
- **3005** – mechanical alignment on the REEF pole, including a retracting mechanism that softens both intake from
  the human-player station and placement on the REEF.
- **1690 vacuum end effector** – very light; great for CORAL, less optimal for the heavy ALGAE.
- **190 feeder intake** – active walls (belts) that also "clap" to straighten CORAL faster.
